A compact one-page rhythm for concise content: a small identity block, short section gaps and efficient dates. Longer resumes must continue naturally rather than clip or shrink.
Use a broad evidence column and a narrow qualifications rail beneath a shallow masthead. Designed to use space efficiently while retaining every section on longer documents.
A low masthead, short rules and compact role lines minimise overhead. Keep the body comfortable and let concise content produce a short document without enforcing a page limit.
Use black type, one fine horizontal rule and an exact shared left edge. Distinguish role, organisation and date with weight and spacing alone.
An intentionally ordinary paper resume with a modest serif name and clean sans body. Avoid ornaments, panels and icons; concentrate on comfortable line lengths and reliable pagination.
Wide outer margins, a small left-aligned identity and relaxed section spacing create an open page. Do not compress long resumes merely to preserve the sparse sample's appearance.
Use a sturdy sans serif, a moderate text measure and clearly separated entries. Keep all essential text dark, links underlined and headings visibly distinct without relying on colour.
Start from a larger body size and generous leading with strong contrast. Reduce decorative overhead rather than text size, and allow additional print pages when needed.
A deliberately narrow central reading measure makes long summaries and achievement bullets easier to follow. Use short blue rules and a small masthead instead of a full-width banner.
Use the available page width with controlled bullet indentation and a compact contact row. Keep very long paragraphs readable through line spacing and clear entry boundaries.
Bring skills and projects ahead of the work chronology with a strong but plain opening. Retain employers and dates so the functional emphasis never conceals career history.
Use an approachable, spacious opening for a summary and current capabilities, followed by an honest chronology. Avoid timeline decorations that overemphasise gaps.
Give education, projects and volunteering useful space before employment. Use a small name, clear section labels and enough breathing room for a genuinely short record.
A slim, light left rail holds practical skills and credentials while education and work examples lead the main column. Empty sections must disappear without leaving a vacant column.
A compact project-forward resume combines a plain identity with monospace metadata. Keep project links and dates text-based and give achievements more space than tool lists.
Small section numbers and a consistent date gutter create an index-like document. Use plenty of white paper and short rules instead of cards or coloured panels.
A single serif family handles the complete resume through careful changes of size and weight. Use no accent colour and only a thin rule beneath the identity.
A clean sans-only page with a compact identity and natural reading order. Role titles are bold, organisation context is regular and dates remain easy to locate.
Move contact links into a tidy right-aligned masthead rail, leaving the career body in one full reading column. Long URLs must wrap at sensible punctuation.
Use two carefully proportioned columns and low-overhead section labels. Preserve all content and body size, with automatic stacking on small screens and continuation on print pages.
Use local-first typography, black rules and conservative page geometry. The document should feel complete with web fonts blocked and should avoid large printed background areas.
A restrained monospace identity and metadata system sits over a highly readable sans body. Use alignment and fine dotted rules instead of terminal effects or fake code.
